title: CTIBench and AthenaBench: the technique head and the group models on two public CTI benchmarks (evaluation only)
question: How do the reference technique head (E2) and the group models (the actor head T1 and the product's TF-IDF text-group model) score on the technique-extraction and threat-actor-attribution tasks of CTIBench and AthenaBench under those benchmarks' own rules?
licences: CTIBench (AI4Sec/cti-bench) CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; AthenaBench (Athena-Software-Group/athenabench) Athena Security Group Academic Research License (non-commercial). Local evaluation only: nothing is trained on them, nothing redistributed, raw files under data/benchmarks/ (gitignored).
harness: scripts/cribl_finetune/external_bench.py (prepare, predict, score); family_head.run_split with the E2 and T1 checkpoints; multi_answer for the up-to-3 variant; apt_classifier.text_group for the TF-IDF baseline; AthenaBench's alias and related-group lists for TAA

rules.ctibench_ate: 60 texts (47 Enterprise, 13 Mobile) split with the product's no-LLM splitter; predicted set = union over sentences of the parent of the sentence's top-1 technique (primary) and of up to three techniques per sentence at 1.3 per sentence (secondary); F1 micro and mean-per-text against the row's parent ids; reported on Enterprise rows and on all rows (the catalogue is Enterprise only, so Mobile rows score 0)
rules.athena_ate: 500 scenarios read whole; accuracy of the top-1 technique at parent level (the benchmark's own rule); top-3 and top-5 at parent level reported
rules.taa: CTIBench 50 reports (answers from the authors' response key) and AthenaBench 100 profiles; the actor head averages each group's probability over the report's sentences (CTIBench) or bullets (AthenaBench) and names the top group; the TF-IDF model scores the whole text; the predicted ATT&CK group's name is scored with AthenaBench's rule: correct when alias-connected to the answer (their alias list plus ATT&CK's names and aliases), plausible when connected through their related-group list, combined = 1 / 0.5 / 0; reported with how many answers map to any ATT&CK group at all
rules.anonymisation: TAA texts additionally pass the actor-name anonymiser used for the actor head ([PLACEHOLDER] and group names -> 'the adversary')

caveats: CTIBench's ATE texts are ATT&CK's own software descriptions and E2 trained on ATT&CK's procedure sentences about the same software: those numbers are flattering. AthenaBench's scenarios are GPT-written from technique descriptions. Actors absent from ATT&CK cannot be named by our models.
success: none registered: a report-only evaluation against the benchmarks' published model scores; no selection, no refit, each model scored once
informed_by: the file formats and the authors' scoring code (athena_eval/evaluate.py); no model has read any of these rows
